Aisha / Hannah — attaching a focused technical artefact that maps Redwood's controls to NIST AI RMF functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and lists the ready artifacts we can produce for evidence: model card, training data lineage summary, model-change log, test harness results, continuous eval dashboards, and KV/prefix caching behaviour notes.

Notes (high level):
- NIST Map -> we provide model lineage and provenance: model_version_id, training_snapshot refs, dataset fingerprints.
- NIST Measure -> continuous evaluation pipeline with scheduled regression runs and drift monitors (statistical and semantic). We store eval results as timestamped artifacts and surface regressions in the console + webhook alerts.
- NIST Manage -> automated rollback / canary policies, model pinning and immutable deploys, and runbook templates for false positives/negatives escalation.
- Evidence artifacts: model_card_v{version}.md, eval-suite-sample.jsonl (attached), regression_history.csv (available on request).

EU AI Act point: for automated credit decisioning you are likely in a high-risk band. Redwood's position: we provide the technical controls and documentation needed to support a conformity assessment, but we are not the conformity assessor. For customers in high-risk uses we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment tied with our Conformity Readiness Package (includes artifact bundling and a 3rd-party assessor contact list).

Attached: redwood-nist-gap-analysis.xlsx (draft), eval-suite-sample.jsonl

Aisha — adding operational controls and readiness notes that specifically map to EU AI Act obligations:

- Human oversight: Redwood supports human-in-loop tooling (review queues, confidence thresholds, and manual-override APIs) and can surface explainability artifacts (influence scores, example-based explanations) per request.
- Transparency & documentation: we maintain model cards, training-data summaries (no raw data export), and change logs. We provide templates for the "technical documentation" that an assessor will expect (architecture diagrams, data flows, risk assessment).
- Data residency: Frankfurt region available for both Hosted (region-specific tenancy) and Dedicated/Private deployments. We can provide KMS integration details and key rotation policies.
- Logging & auditability: per-request tracing including model_version_id, input_hash, output_hash, latency, and cost; logs stored with configurable retention (default 90 days, extendable).

On eval/regression cadence: default recommendation for credit risk is nightly full-regression with hourly monitors for drift on production traffic. Metrics we typically report: AUC/ROC (if applicable), Precision@k for top-k tasks, calibration error, fairness metrics by protected cohort, distributional drift (KL), semantic similarity drift, and perplexity-like perplexity only for LM tasks.

I can produce a 1-page "Conformity Readiness Checklist" for your assessor that maps EU AI Act clauses to artifacts and culpability owners.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Compliance — Redwood Inference
